How $obs is transformed before being plotted as a bar height: "none" = raw counts; "log" = log1p(obs) (natural log of obs+1, not a bare log(obs), so a night with 0 observations doesn't break the axis); "log10" = log10(obs+1). Overridable per-plot via fig.list's own $Yaxe.trans. See this function's @details for how this was verified against Josh's target image.

Only has an effect when $Yaxe.trans is "log"/"log10": FALSE (default) labels each Y-axis break with the real $obs-scale number (e.g. 100); TRUE labels it with the transformed value instead (e.g. 4.6). Overridable per-plot via fig.list's own $loglabels.

Which raw values become Y-axis breaks: "regular" (default - see notes below) places them at the exact 0/25/50/75/100% points of 0-$ymax; "rounded" places them at those same four points but rounds each to the nearest whole number first; "custom" uses the exact numbers in $y.custom instead, ignoring the 0/25/50/75/100% computation entirely. Overridable per-plot via fig.list's own $y.scale. NOTE: Josh's original spec marked both "regular" and "rounded" as "(default)" - almost certainly a copy/paste slip, since only one can be the real default; "regular" was picked here (listed first, simpler reading) - please confirm.
